directAnswer: You can check your monitor's refresh rate through your operating system's display settings. The steps vary slightly between Windows and macOS.
summary: This guide provides steps to check the refresh rate of your monitor on different operating systems.

sections.heading: Checking Refresh Rate on Windows
sections.body: To check the refresh rate on Windows, you can access the display settings through the Settings app.

sections.heading: Checking Refresh Rate on macOS
sections.body: On macOS, you can find the refresh rate settings in the Displays section of System Preferences.

steps.title: Windows 10/11
steps.detail: Right-click on the desktop, select 'Display settings', scroll down to 'Advanced display settings', and check the refresh rate under 'Refresh rate'.

steps.title: macOS
steps.detail: Click the Apple menu, go to 'System Preferences', select 'Displays', and hold the Option key while clicking 'Scaled' to see the refresh rate options.

faqs.question: What is a refresh rate?
faqs.answer: The refresh rate refers to how many times per second the display updates the image, measured in Hertz (Hz).

faqs.question: Can I change my monitor's refresh rate?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your monitor supports higher refresh rates, you can change it in the display settings, but it must be compatible with your graphics card.

faqs.question: Why is my refresh rate lower than expected?
faqs.answer: A lower refresh rate may occur due to limitations in the cable used, the monitor's settings, or the capabilities of your graphics card.

caveats: The steps may vary slightly depending on your operating system version and hardware configuration.
